short: New 2-D CNN front end (0 of 110 prior decoders) but an unrepeated gain (M06 standard); test-word frames trained the CNN, inflating its PCA comparison (M12 behind).
position: The paper [@noda2014lipreading] changes the visual front end (M06): a CNN on mouth images emits 40 phoneme posteriors for a GMM-HMM. No CNN appears among the 110 prior lip-reading decoders (pattern match, Appendix), but a shared-weight network on lip pixels [@duchnowski1994see], network phoneme posteriors in HMMs [@heckmann2001hybrid] and learned mouth features [@ngiam2011multimodal] came first; only spatial convolution is new. M06 is standard: the word gain over PCA is one unrepeated comparison (Sec. 6.3). Evaluation (M12) is behind because the CNN was trained on image sequences from all 300 words (Sec. 4), so the 84 test words are unseen only by the HMM, whereas the best comparable prior fits every stage on training data [@duchnowski1994see]; the authors' "closed-speaker" test (Sec. 6.3) was common then [@cox2008challenge]. The strongest confound follows: only the CNN was fitted, with labels, on test-word frames, so exposure and supervision both favour it over unsupervised PCA.
